title: Multi-Dimensional SLO Triage and Prioritization Playbook
author: Aisha Gomez
content:
## Overview

Purpose: This playbook defines a repeatable, multi-dimensional process for triaging SLO violations, prioritizing remediation work, and applying error-budget-aware capacity decisions. It is intended for oncall engineers, SRE leads, and product partners responsible for service reliability and capacity investment.

Audience: oncall, SRE, platform, service owners, product managers.

Scope: applies to all Redwood public-facing inference APIs and internal supporting services that have SLOs defined in the central SLO registry. Not intended for emergent security incidents (see security incident playbook).

---

## Key concepts and definitions

- SLO dimensionality: We consider three orthogonal axes when evaluating an SLO event: User Impact, Frequency, and Cost/Capacity Risk. Each axis has explicit criteria below.
- Error budget: The remaining allowable fraction of user-facing failure within the SLO window. Error budget spend drives remediation urgency and rollback decisions.
- Triage window: 30 minutes for initial assessment, 2 hours for stabilization plan, 24 hours for remediation plan.

---

## SLO evaluation matrix (summary)

| Axis | Low | Medium | High |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| User impact | Single-user or dev-facing; degraded logs | Group of customers; increased latency for non-critical routes | Broad customer-facing failures; failed generation responses |
| Frequency | 1–5 errors/hour | 6–50 errors/hour | >50 errors/hour or sustained >1% error rate |
| Cost/Capacity risk | No capacity pressure; autoscaling healthy | Moderate GPU surge or queueing; autoscale compensating | Saturated GPU pools, queued requests >30s, risk of cascading failures |

Guidance: treat any "High" in User impact OR Cost/Capacity risk as high-priority regardless of frequency.

---

## Prioritization rubric (scoring)

Assign numeric scores and sum to rank work. Use this for post-triage backlog prioritization and for deciding automated mitigations.

- User impact: Low=1, Medium=3, High=6
- Frequency: Low=1, Medium=2, High=4
- Cost/Capacity risk: Low=0, Medium=2, High=5
- Business criticality multiplier: non-critical=1.0, core-platform=1.5, enterprise-SLA=2.0

Priority score = (User + Frequency + Capacity) * Multiplier

Interpretation:
- 0–4: low priority (document and schedule normal work)
- 5–11: medium priority (address within sprint; monitor closely)
- 12+: high priority (immediate action, possible rollback/fallback)

---

## Triage workflow (step-by-step)

1. Alert claims and initial assessment (0–30 minutes)
   - Responsible: oncall responder.
   - Actions: confirm alert fidelity, correlate with SLO dashboards and recent deploys, determine dimensions (User impact, Frequency, Capacity).
   - CLI snippets:
     - Check SLO dashboard: curl -s https://observability.internal/api/slo?service=<SERVICE>
     - Query Prometheus for error rate (last 5m):
       - prometheus: rate(request_errors_total{service="<SERVICE>"}[5m]) / rate(request_total{service="<SERVICE>"}[5m])
2. Rapid containment (0–2 hours)
   - Responsible: oncall + service owner.
   - Actions: apply mitigations to reduce user impact: feature-flag to degrade non-essential work, enable cached responses, route to replica region, apply circuit-breaker settings. Document all actions in the incident ticket.
3. Prioritization decision (within 2 hours)
   - Responsible: oncall lead + SRE oncall + product representative (if high business impact).
   - Actions: compute priority score, decide if immediate rollback or capacity expansion is required, invoke automated runbooks if appropriate.
4. Stabilize and handoff (2–24 hours)
   - Create a remediation ticket with acceptance criteria, owner, and ETA. Schedule a short (15–30 min) sync if high-priority. Ensure error budget tracking entry is created.
5. Remediation and retrospective (24h+)
content_continued:
- Implement permanent fix, run regression tests, and coordinate rollout with canary if needed. After remediation, run a lightweight post-mortem and update the SLO registry if thresholds or measurement windows change.

---

## Automated decision thresholds and runbooks

- Auto-throttle: if latency P95 > 1200ms for >5 minutes AND queued requests >50 per replica, trigger auto-throttle policy (reduce concurrency limit by 30%, enable short-circuit for heavy routes).
- Emergency capacity scale: if GPU utilization > 92% for >10 minutes across the cluster AND error rate >0.5%, automatically scale dedicated pools by one shard (subject to committed capacity caps).

Runbook examples (Kubernetes):
- Scale pool: kubectl patch gdeploy inference-pool -p '{"spec":{"replicas":<N>}}'
- Disable route via feature flag: curl -X POST https://ff-admin.internal/flags -d '{"key":"/routes/heavy","enabled":false}'

PromQL examples:
- Service error rate (5m): sum(rate(http_request_errors_total{service="<svc>"}[5m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{service="<svc>"}[5m]))
- Queue depth: sum(queue_depth{service="<svc>"}) by (instance)

---

## Ticket template (use exactly this format)

Title: [SLO TRIAGE] <SERVICE> — <SHORT DESCRIPTION>
Labels: incident, slo-triage, <service>, <priority>
Severity: P1/P2/P3 (choose based on priority score)
Impact summary: <one-line user facing impact>
Initial triage (who/when): <oncall> — <timestamp>
User-impact: Low/Medium/High
Frequency: Low/Medium/High
Capacity risk: Low/Medium/High
Immediate mitigation steps taken: <list>
Owner for remediation: <team/person>
Estimated time to remediation: <ETA>
Post-incident actions: create postmortem within 72 hours, update test/alerting, verify rollback conditions

---

## Post-incident standards and evidence collection

- Postmortem must include: timeline, root cause, contributing factors, remediation actions, roll-forward/rollback decision rationale, and owners.
- Evidence to attach: relevant query results, console snapshots of autoscaling actions, feature-flag events, deploy IDs, and link to ticket.
- Postmortem owner: incident commander or assigned service owner. Due within 72 hours for P1/P2; 7 days for P3.

---

## Capacity planning integration

- Use priority scores aggregated over a rolling 90-day window to influence capacity purchases and reserved pool sizing.
- Quarterly run: SRE + capacity planning run a scoring review and convert recurring medium/high scores into capacity requests or deferred-optimization tasks.
- Example threshold: if a service records >3 Medium/High priority events in 90 days attributable to capacity, create a Reserved Capacity request ticket.

---

## Observability and dashboard checklist

Each SLO-tracked service must expose:
- Error rate (1m, 5m, 1h)
- Latency percentiles (p50, p95, p99) by route/class
- Queue depth and processing backlog
- Replica GPU utilization and memory pressure
- Recent deploy IDs and rollback markers

Include links in the ticket to the precise dashboard panels and to the SLO measurement query.

---

## Ownership and escalation

- Primary: service owner (team listed in service registry)
- Secondary: platform SRE oncall
- Escalation path: oncall -> oncall lead -> SRE manager -> Head of SRE -> CTO (for enterprise-impacting escalations).

Contact policy: if an event is classified High and not improving within 15 minutes of mitigation, page the product manager and account success for affected enterprise customers.

---

## Change control and periodic review

- This playbook must be reviewed annually and after any P1 event.
- Changes that affect automation thresholds require a changelog entry and a single-author approval plus one reviewer.

Change log:
- 2026-01-15: Added emergency capacity scale automation and clarified scoring multiplier for enterprise customers. (Aisha Gomez)
- 2025-02-12: Initial publication. (Aisha Gomez)

---

## Appendix: quick checklists

Initial 30-minute checklist:
- [ ] Confirm alert is not a duplicate or stale.
- [ ] Identify deploys in the last 30 minutes.
- [ ] Compute user/frequency/capacity axes.
- [ ] Document initial mitigation steps in ticket.

2-hour stabilization checklist:
- [ ] Decide on rollback vs mitigation vs capacity scale.
- [ ] If rollback, document rollback ID and revert plan.
- [ ] If scale, confirm autoscaling actions and capacity limits.

24-hour remediation checklist:
- [ ] Remediation owner assigned and ETA set.
- [ ] Postmortem owner and timeline created.
- [ ] SLO registry updated if necessary.

For questions or training requests, contact the SRE Enablement channel on Slack (#sre-enable) or the SRE team wiki page.
